answer: The $90 carbon tax option combined with sectoral investments would reduce emissions by 42.8 percent relative to the BAU scenario by 2030 [ccdr:p045:pypdf:03]. Under the net-zero pathway (NZP), Vietnam’s GDP would be 0.6 percent lower in 2030 than in the BAU scenario [ccdr:p045:pypdf:03].

citations.text: Combined with sectoral investments, the $90 tax would reduce emissions by 42.8 percent relative to the BAU scenario by 2030, and 73.6 percent by 2040. The reduction would mainly be driven by the gradual increase in the carbon tax, technology shifts in manufacturing/ trade, and the transition of the energy sector away from coal. The power sector would make the greatest contributions to GHG emission reductions, followed by manufacturing, transport, and agriculture. Pursuing the net-zero pathway could slow GDP growth. The CGE model shows that under the NZP, Vietnam’s GDP would be 0.6 percent lower in 2030 and 2.2 percent lower in 2040 than in the BAU scenario (a description of main assumptions and key results can be found in Annex 3).

answer: The current Environmental Protection Tax on gasoline is $77.60 per tCO2e [ccdr:p022:pypdf:00], which is significantly higher than the $12 per tCO2e starting level of the most modest economy-wide carbon tax option analyzed [ccdr:p045:pypdf:02].

citations.text: 12 Vietnam Country Climate and Development Report The new strategies have yet to be translated into significant changes in Vietnam’s fiscal policy. For example, some progress has been made toward the development of carbon pricing instruments, but such instruments are not yet implemented at scale. The existing carbon tax — the Environmental Protection Tax (EPT) — is around $0.50 per tCO2e on coal, $77.60 per tCO2e on gasoline, and $32.90 per tCO2e on diesel, lower than most countries and too low to incentivize large-scale decarbonization.

Those investments alone would reduce GHG emissions by nine percent in 2030 and 21 percent in 2040 relative to a BAU scenario. However, that is far short of what is required to achieve net zero by 2050. Sectoral investments will need to be supported by carbon pricing (as a tax or through regulations creating an emission trading system) to incentivize businesses and households to shift their behaviors toward low-emitting activities.55 Several options were analyzed for an economywide carbon tax . The most modest option would start at about $12 per tCO 2e in 2022, which is the weighted average of the EPT rate on coal, diesel, and gasoline, and ramp up to $40 per tCO2e by 2040. The two other options are to ramp up to $90 or to $120 per tCO2e by 2040 (from the same starting point). The $90 option appears sufficient to generate the necessary changes in emitting activities.

citations.text: The main beneficiaries have been agriculture, renewable energy, sustainable water management, and sustainable forestry. The lack of internal procedures for and expertise on green finance assessment is a key challenge for many banks.
